l.i: Aristotelis mentem, sententiam: Ex ijs quæ dicta sunt
cōficitur, cum neq; unum principium sufficiat, neq;
duo, deinde non opus sit ponere quatuor aut plura:
rectè definiri, tria esse principia rerum naturaliū, &
neq; plura neq; pauciora.
Quia in quarumcunq; rerum naturalium pro-
ductione tria inter se distincta cōcurrunt ut nece-
ssaria & sufficientia. Sunt autem hæc, materia, for-
ma, & priuatio.
Duabus rationibus. Prima: Omne quod fit, aut
fit simpliciter, id est, efficitur substantia: aut fit non
simpliciter, id est, acquirit quoddā accidēs. Sed neu-
tro horum modorū aliquid fit, nisi præstò sit mate-
ria, seu nisi aliquid subijciatur. Igitur ad productio-
nem rerum naturalium necessaria est materia. Mi-
nor probatur. Nam si quid fit simpliciter, aliquid
quidem necessario subijcitur: quandoquidem forma
aduenire non potest, nisi ubi subiecta est materia:
forma semper præexhibet materiam. Si aliquid au-
tem fiat non simpliciter, tum multò magis oportet
subiectum seu materia aliqua ut adsit. Reuera enim
accidens acquiri nullum potest, nisi adsit subie-
ctum

page.notes: Page number read as "86"; the top-left figure is partly faded. The running head shows only "AND. HYPERII"; the start of the title before it is cut off or faded, so I left it out. The line-end hyphen "subie-" is continued by "ctum" on the next line, which I read as "ctum" (the c and t are joined in print). Long s is set as plain s throughout. The first word "Aristotelis" begins a paragraph continued from the previous page. The "Confirmatio." line is a set-apart lead line and is given as a level 2 heading. The question heading "Quomodo demonstras..." is centred over three lines. The top-left "a6" and the Aristotelian quotation marks are not printed text. The "Quia" opening carries an underlined Q in print, which I have written as plain Q.
